translations.answer: Maintainers first provided principles: if kMt is the placement of the tip frame relative to the knee joint frame, then the single Force should be acted upon using kMt.act(f_t), and not the entire vector<Force>. The original author ultimately adopted the explicitly referenced OCS2 commit 3566993: finding the parent joint of the contact frame, rotating the world-frame force using data.oMi[jointIndex].rotation().transpose(), taking the linear component as the force, and the angular component as the joint-to-contact translation multiplied by the force. A 6-DoF contact also includes the rotated contact torque, and the model.njoints length of fext is passed to rnea. The author confirmed that the original issue was resolved.
translations.applicability: Applicable to original post floating-base quadruped, foot contact frame, and original author's reference OCS2 3566993; other contact metadata and wrench convention must be revalidated.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue is closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict. It has formal documentation or independent reproducible exact references.
translations.details.attempts.0: Maintainer suggests kMt.act(f_t)；author then uses OCS2 to fix the parent-joint force/wrench in the submission.
translations.details.attempts.1: Another participant manually formulated floating base equations using CRBA, nonLinearEffects, and frame Jacobians, and compared the results with those from rnea.
translations.details.attempts.2: Participants discussed the solution boundaries for single-contact re-rooting and multi-contact acceleration-level holonomic constraints.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Find the parent joint of the contact frame and the relative placement between the two, then transform the wrench to the local frame of the joint.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Distinguish between a single force element and the length of model.njoints in the force vector.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Compare the handwritten floating base equations with rnea output and evaluate separately whether kinematic-tree sparsity was utilized.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Establish the 'fext' element based on the parent joint of the contact frame, rotate the world-frame force to the joint frame, and construct the moment using joint-to-contact translation × force; for 6D contact, add the joint-frame contact torque.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: Apply the transformation to a single pinocchio::Force instead of a aligned_vector<Force>.
translations.details.environments.0: 2022 Pinocchio C++；floating-base quadruped；foot-tip contact frames；author used the CentroidalModelRbdConversions.cpp from OCS2 commit 3566993
translations.details.limits.0: Original author's OCS2 code is based on specific centroidal input and contact metadata; prior to copying, one must verify the frame parent, wrench order, and coordinate expression.
translations.details.limits.1: The thread does not provide specific release, numerical error, or runtime measurement for Pinocchio.
translations.details.limits.2: Discussions regarding re-rooting, Schur complement, and TSID in multi-contact scenarios are architectural suggestions and not implemented in this thread.
translations.details.limits.3: The original author's statement regarding the omission of the first six dimensions depends on their system interpretation, and the thread has not verified it as a universal operation for all floating-base robots.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Original author confirmed that the original problem was resolved after adopting the OCS2 code.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The original author reported results from hand-written floating base equations and rnea that are very close, but no error or speed reference was provided.
translations.details.outcomes.2: No implementation retest was provided for the QP/TSID design discussion in this thread.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When the foot contact frame does not have joints, how to construct a model.njoints length and express the rnea force in the joint local frame?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Does direct use of CRBA, nonLinearEffects, and frame Jacobian result in equivalent and efficient torque calculations compared to RNEA?
translations.details.problem_statements.2: Can multiple fixed contact points be handled by setting one of them as the RNEA root?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Verify the sign of fext, reference point of torque, frame transform, and unactuated base dynamics residual before commanding torque in an embodied robot.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Directly input the contact-frame force into RNEA without converting the action point and local expression.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Calling SE3 action on a whole std::vector<Force>.
translations.details.suspected_causes.2: The handwritten dense CRBA/Jacobian calculations did not utilize the RNEA's motion tree recursive sparse structure.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The 'rnea' requires the local-frame force exerted on each joint, but physical contact occurs at the foot-tip frame of a joint that does not have a corresponding joint.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Directly calling SE3 act on aligned_vector<Force> causes a compilation error, indicating that the vector lacks a se3Action method.
